episodes.165074: An arctic cold front approached and passed through the area February 3rd into February 4th. Multiple waves of low pressure moved along this front, allowing for a slow moving system which provided plenty of rainfall, heavy at times, to the Ohio Valley and across West Virginia. Widespread precipitation accumulations of 2 to 3 inches fell with this system with isolated amounts of 3 to 3 and a half inches along the Ohio River in northwest West Virginia, which led to numerous flooding issues across the area. In addition to the rainfall, snowmelt from previous systems also assisted with causing flooding issues for the region.||Multiple rivers exceeded flood stage within West Virginia, the most notable along Middle Island Creek at Middlebourne and Little, West Virginia, where major flooding occurred along Routes 18 and 24. This also led to the buildings at the 4H campground near Middlebourne to flood, as well as the Tyler County fairgrounds. Many roadways throughout West Virginia were closed due to high water and water flowed into multiple residences in Harrison County. Additionally, in Ritchie County, the body of an elderly man was found after being swept away by floodwaters from the Hughes River flowing out of its banks.

Flooding occurred in multiple residential homes and campgrounds due to rivers and creeks flowing out of their banks.

episodes.165453: What began as a flooding event transitioned into a winter weather event as rain transitioned to a wintry mix during the afternoon and evening of February 3rd as an arctic cold front crossed through the Ohio Valley. Warmer air at the upper levels allowed for freezing rain to occur along southeast Ohio. Areas of over a quarter of an inch of ice accretion occurred, with some localized higher amounts up to around four tenths of an inch of ice observed.||The wintry mix of precipitation transitioned to snow late on February 3rd into early February 4th where snowfall accumulations of around 1 to 3 inches fell along southeast Ohio. A second wave of light snowfall moved in late on February 4th into the morning of February 5th where an additional 1 to 3 inches of snowfall fell. The freezing rain had the most significant impact with this system, leading to numerous power outages and tree damage along the northern portions of southeast Ohio. Morgan County had widespread power outages which led to significant disruptions in communication.
episodes.166173: Low pressure passing to the west of the region ushered in anomalously moist airmass and resultant heavy rain and flooding.
episodes.166304: A highly unstable and moist atmosphere promoted heavy rainfall over portions of west central and northeast Georgia as several disturbances traversed a stalled frontal boundary. Several reports of flash flooding were relayed in the early morning hours as rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches fell quickly over west central Georgia.
episodes.166444: The field of moisture associated with a frontal boundary promoted a prolonged rainfall event across the area. Many areas received 3 to 6 inches with maximum around 10 inches. This resulted in several flooding events across the area.
episodes.166495: A slow moving cold front moved through Central Alabama during the afternoon and overnight hours on February 3-4. A supercell thunderstorm developed in far eastern Mississippi and produced three EF2 tornadoes as it moved across west Alabama. Additional storms produced 2 EF0 tornadoes in Elmore County.  A line of storms stalled along and south of the Interstate 85 corridor, resulting in a period of heavy rainfall and flash flooding.  Rainfall totals of 4-6 inches were observed over a 3 hour period.
episodes.166563: Periods of mostly light to moderate rain spread across eastern Kentucky on February 2nd and February 3rd, as waves of low pressure rode along a slow-moving arctic cold front settling in from the northwest. The strongest and last wave of low pressure lifted across the Appalachians late February 3rd and into February 4th bringing with it a final round of rain, changing over to a wintry mix and eventually snow flurries across eastern Kentucky. While 2-day rainfall amounts ranged from 1.5 to 3.0 inches across much of the area, rainfall rates were low, and only minor flooding was reported, closing several roadways. Rivers reached elevated stages, but only the Red River at Clay City exceeded minor flood stage, spilling across farm fields and low-lying roadways. ||This system also produced heavy icing at many locations along and north of I-64. South of I-64, heavy icing became increasingly confined to the higher ridges with southeastward extent. The shallow cold layer with the cold front quickly moved into the Bluegrass on the morning of February 3rd, causing thermometers to fall to near freezing north of I-64 and along the southeast rim of the Bluegrass (down to around western Jackson and northern Rockcastle counties). Some limited daytime heating seemed to keep temperatures just warm enough for plain rain through much the day, but after sunset temperatures cooled just enough for icing to begin. The marginally sub-freezing temperatures and moderate rainfall rates led to runoff and inefficient ice accretion. Further southeast, the shallow cold layer struggled to make much progress into the East Kentucky Coalfield during the day; instead, temperatures largely held in the 40s and 50s through the afternoon. During the evening, the cold layer became deep enough to surge southeastward, bringing with it sub-freezing temperatures to the ridgetops. By the time precipitation tapered off early February 4th, an icy glaze coated the Southeast Bluegrass and many of the higher east Kentucky Coalfield ridges. Very slippery road conditions were reported as far south as Jackson County, and Fleming County issued a Level 2 Weather Emergency due to the hazardous road conditions.  However, many of the Coalfield Valleys of southeast Kentucky remained just above freezing until after the rain ended, thus preventing notable icing.
episodes.166883: A very moist and unstable airmass developed ahead of an approaching cold front. Storms developed along the front and produced damaging wind gusts as they moved across southeast Mississippi and southwest Alabama. Heavy rain caused flooding across portions of the area.
episodes.166888: A cold front across the local area during the afternoon hours of February 3rd. A  thunderstorm along this boundary intensified as it passed across Lake Pontchartrain. It produced strong wind gusts as it crossed the Causeway and Lakefront Airport. No damage noted with these storms.
episodes.166932: Warm temperatures and rainfall resulted in an ice jam on Penns Creek in the Millmont area of Union County.
episodes.167131: The combination of a deep, slow moving upper-level trough across the West Coast and a cold high pressure over the Midwest created the perfect setup for a Winter Storm/Ice Storm/flooding scenario in portions of the Ohio River Valley. The frontal boundary stalled across our County Warning Area and depending on which side of the frontal boundary you were you located you either saw heavy ice, snow, or rainfall.

events.narrative: Heavy rain caused a portion of SR 146 to close due to high water.

Several roads in the county were closed due to flooding on the evening of February 3rd. These included State Route 145, State Route 821, and State Route 26. They would remain closed into the next day while high water issues were observed.
Multiple reports of Flash Flooding in the Monroeville area. Also reports of homes flooding in the area.
Heavy rain caused several roads throughout the county to close due to flooding.

Middle Island Creek near Middlebourne rose out of its 16 foot bankfull level on the evening of February 3rd, crested at around 23 feet on the afternoon of the 4th, and returned to its banks during the early morning hours on the 5th. This resulted in major flooding along Route 18 and Route 24 on either side of the river. The buildings at the nearby 4H campground were also flooded, as well as the Tyler County fairgrounds.

On the evening of February 3rd, the Little Muskingum River near Bloomfield rose above its 16 foot bankfull level. The river crested at 23.53 feet on the afternoon of the 4th and then receded back its its banks just after midnight early on the 5th. While out of its banks, Bloomfield Church Lane near the bridge flooded.
KY-1527 was reported blocked due to flood waters between mile markers 0 and 1 near the community of Baileys Switch.
The Weatherflow Mesonet on Lake Pontchartrain Causeway at Mid Lake measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 37 knots or 42 mph.
Heavy rain caused State Highway 21 at Bailey Road to be impassable.
Heavy rain caused numerous roads to be damaged or washed out due to flash flooding.
A vehicle overturned in Limestone Creek with entrapment off of Highway 41 north of Monroeville. Numerous roads are flooded and impassable in the area.
Flooding occurred along several portions of Kentucky Route 5.
High water occurred over the road near the intersection of Blackburn Avenue and Roberts Drive near the city of Ashland.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding on Parker Lane in Uriah.
The downtown Monroeville fire department is flooded with a significant amount of water in the building.
Heavy rain caused the area near the intersection of Seven Pines and Brink roads to flood.
Heavy rain caused a portion of Huskey Highway to close due to flooding.
Several low-lying roads flooded in Marion County due to heavy rainfall.
Significant flash flooding west of Greenville. Portions of CR 38 North and Hawkins Lane were completely washed out.
Bookers Mill Road was washed out from flash flooding. Numerous dirt roads were also washed out.
KY-711 near the community of Wrigley was reported as being blocked due to flood waters, between mile markers 3 and 4.
High water was observed along Old Lick Creek Road.
Roads flooded and impassable which include Perryman and County Road 37.
KY-52 was reported being blocked due to floodwaters between mile markers 0 and 2 in Lee County.

Duck Creek near Whipple rose out of its 12 foot bankfull level late in the night on February 3rd. The creek reached just above 15 feet on the afternoon of the 4th before returning to its banks just before dawn on the 5th. While the creek was out of its banks, portions of State Routes 26, 821, and 145 flooded.

In the town of Whipple, Duck Creek rose out of its 12 foot bankfull level late on the evening of February 3rd. The creek crested at 15.39 feet the next afternoon then returned to its banks during the predawn hours of February 5th. Minor flooding occurred along State Routes 26, 821, and 145 while Duck Creek was out of its banks.

Middle Island Creek near the town of Little rose out of its 14 foot bankfull level just before midnight on February 3rd. It would not return to its banks until the late morning hours on the 5th. The river crested at 21.46 feet, which resulted in water to reach private cabins that reside near the waterway close to the Friendly Road bridge.
Several roads flooded and impassable, including portions of Highway 110, County Road 185, and Jack Griswold Road.
Numerous roads flooded and impassable in areas south of Interstate 85. Roads impacted include 2, 10, 23, 36, 13 and Highway 29.
Heavy rain caused a portion of SR260 to be closed due to flooding.

The Shade River near Chester rose out of its 17 foot bankfull level late on the evening of February 3rd. The river crested at 23.33 feet and returned to its banks just before noon on the 5th. While out of its banks, the Shade River spilled onto Oak Hill Road upstream from the Shade River Bridge.
Multiple streets flooded in Huntington, including 12th Street and Enslow Boulevard.
Hurricane Creek rose out of its banks and spilled onto Harbour Lane in the town of Hurricane. In Winfield, flooding was observed along Tucker Branch.
Flooding was observed near the 1900 Block along South State Highway 1.
High water flowed along Brush Creek Road near the 1600 Block.
Several roads flooded and impassable south of I-85. Uchee Creek out of its banks and into homes along Lee Road 2103.  Lee Road 146 flooded and impassable west of Highway 169.
Heavy rain caused a portion of SR26 to close due to flooding.
Heavy rain caused the area by SR564 and SR145 to close due to flooding.
High water flowed along Buffalo Branch Road.
Several roads reported flooded and impassable.  Sandfort Road washed out where it crosses over Uchee Creek.

Red Lick Road (KY-3328) was reported blocked due to flooding between mile markers 0 and 1.3.
In Spencer, Bell Street and Front Street flooded. High water was also observed along Locust Street in Reedy.
High water occurred over the intersection of Trace Road and Four Mile Road.
High water was observed over Walnut Street along US Route 23 in the city of Catlettsburg.

An ice jam on Penns Creek led to the rescue of several people Friday morning in the Millmont area of Union County. No injuries were reported after two people and a dog were rescued from a house surrounded by water of Penns Creek.||According to the Mifflinburg Hose Company Facebook page, crews were called to the 900 block of Canada Drive in Lewis Township, Union County just after 5:30 a.m. Friday.

Symmes Creek in the town of Aid rose above its 19 foot bankfull level on the morning of February 4th, cresting that evening around 21.5 feet. The creek did not return to its banks until the late evening hours two days later. While out of its banks, minor flooding was observed near residential homes in close proximity to the creek.

The Emergency Manager reported the bridge on Wallace Road between Robert Williams Road and Chipley Highway was flooded from a nearby lake.  Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 4 inches of rain occurred quickly over the area during the overnight period, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported Mobley Road washed out at Little Branch. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
KY-2013 was reported blocked due to flood waters in the community of Jenson.
Heavy rain caused Buffalo run to rise out of its banks and flood New Stanton Ruffsdale Road, leading to a vehicle becoming stuck in high water.

In the town of Mill Creek, the Tygart Valley River rose above its 11 foot bankfull level just before sunrise on the 4th, cresting at 12.24 around noon, then returned to its banks late that evening. Backwater from the river spilled onto portions of Route 39 while out of its banks.
Heavy rain caused Sewickly Creek to flood onto East Hillis Street, with evidence of water higher than wheels of vehicles.

Near the town of West Union, Middle Island Creek rose out of its 16 foot bankfull level around sunrise on the 4th. The river crested at 17.75 feet just before noon and returned to its banks shortly afterwards. Minor flooding was observed along Route 18.
KY-1527 was reported blocked due to flooding in the area between mile markers 2 and 2.4 in the community of Baileys Switch.

Sewickly Creek ran out of its banks near the intersection of Amburst Brinkerton and Udell roads due to heavy rainfall. This caused a vehicle to become trapped in flood water, resulting in a water rescue.
Heavy rain causing Sewickly Creek to rise out of its banks flooded the area near the intersection of Creek Road and Derr Road.
Heavy rain caused flooding along low lying areas of Loyalhanna creek.

In Grayson, the Little Sandy River rose above its 21 foot flood stage, crested at 22.04 feet later that afternoon, then returned to its banks in the evening. This resulted in high water issues along Route 773, State Route 1910, and around the Dixie Park area just past the I-64 bridge.
KY-225 was blocked due to flooding in the area at mile marker 4, near the community of Kayjay.
Heavy rain resulted in the Loyalhanna Creek rising such that the area of Route 982 between Route 30 and Mission Rd were closed due to flooding.

The body of an elderly man was found after being swept away by floodwaters due to Hughes River being out of its banks. The vehicle was spotted by passing motorists near State Route 47 in the Cisco area nearly submerged underwater.

In the town of Enterprise, the West Fork River rose out of its 17 foot bankfull level on the morning of February 4th. The river crested at 19.66 feet that evening and returned to its banks a few hours after midnight on the 5th. High water occurred during this time along roads located nearby to the gage.
Heavy rain caused an Ice Jam Flood that resulted in the Muskingum backing up and flooding into homes along Riverside Airport road.

The river returned to its banks two hours later, cresting a few inches above 12 feet before receding.
